text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Tuesday morning newspapers:
- A Slovenian delegation attends three-day succession talks which started in Brussels on Monday between successor states of former Yugoslavia. The talks are led by mediator Arthur Watts.
- Slovenia's April industrial output rose by 4.3 percent compared to the same month last year, the statistical office reported on Monday.
- Over 160 exhibitors from 12 countries are taking part in the 43rd International Wine Fair that started in Ljubljana on Monday.
- Slovenian Motorway Company (DARS) said maintenance of Slovenian motorways will cost 1.67 billion tolars ($10.7 million) this year and reconstruction of damaged facilities 1.75 billion tolars.

- Talks between railway workers and management are set to continue on Tuesday. Railway unions say they will continue their strike, which ended on Saturday, next Thursday if their demands for higher wages are not met by then.
- A 12-member delegation of Slovenia's ministry of defence, led by Defence Minister Tit Turnsek meets U.S. Secretary of Defence William Cohen on Tuesday.
